status: PARTIAL — canvas verified at every viewport; ring side and Cosmos entry framing fixed and proven; an autonomous spatial camera pose remains an open blocker
canvasVerdict: The surface, drawing buffer, camera aspect and fov agree at every viewport. WP02's 'canvas stuck at 384x661' was a measurement artifact: the Cloud browser panel re-applies its viewport between tool calls.

rootCause.primary: WP02's ring depth (+7.2) put every object on the viewer's side of the resting camera (z 6.8, or sampled poses like (0,1.5,5)/(6,2.5,4)), 32 m past the core at z=-25; objects projected off-screen (screen x -542..-10583, inFrustum false) while the sky and core painted.
rootCause.secondary: The home orb's 'Look at the Cosmos' opened the Cosmos without requesting object framing, unlike the dock and the tool.
rootCause.open: useSpatialCamera writes camera position/target/fov whenever SpatialRuntime reports a transition (SpatialExperience calls runtime.start('core') on mount), overriding object framing and the user's orbit.

fix.migration: legacyRingSignature distinguishes 'cluster' (v1) from 'behind-camera' (v2); repairs are recorded as 'auto-placed' so they are never mistaken for a user move; v2's shipped 'relocated / placement v1 → v2' entries are still read as store moves
fix.entry: CosmosHome orb now issues cosmosViewBus.request({mode:'open', frame:true}), the same request the dock and the tool use
fix.hazards: setHazards(source, hazards) keeps per-source volumes; room markers publish from src/core/cosmos/roomHazards.ts (ROOMS_Z_OFFSET -25, drawn radii 1.2/0.7/0.4 + tube 0.05)
fix.openSlot: widens to 24 rings instead of falling back to an unchecked slot (a failing test caught the old fallback landing inside a 20 m hazard)

openBlocker.observed: camera moved (-0.02,1.5,5) → (6,2.5,4) → (0.2,7.58,23.67) → (-1.37,1.79,2.97) → (6,2.5,4) with no user input, moving objects out of frame after framing
consequence: a capture can still show an empty Cosmos
taps can land where an object was
openBlocker.state: NOT FIXED — camera authority question, belongs in its own work package

limitations: Chromium viewport emulation only; no physical iPhone/iPad
pointer selection not proven end-to-end: the spatial pose moved the camera between probe and click
resize-after-remount measured only as canvas/aspect (same numbers as a live resize); the pose drift masks visual confirmation
the two objects a user had relocated remain on the far side by design and are only visible once framed
